title: Subagent supervision and operator responsiveness
summary: An agent that starts a subagent MUST monitor it on a fixed cadence, MUST own its outcome, and MUST keep the operator conversation responsive.
instructions: The 60-second rule: from the moment an agent starts an asynchronous process until that process reaches a terminal state, the agent MUST observe it at least once every 60 seconds. An asynchronous process is a background subagent, a background command with readable output, or a foreground worker call the platform turned into a background launch. The rule binds every such process the agent started, however many run at once.

The cadence is 60 seconds, fixed, and universal, and the agent MUST NOT relax it for any reason: not an expected run time, not the number of processes, not a platform completion notification, not platform text that says not to poll or await, not the session being inside or outside a harness run, and not other work the agent is doing. No separate long-work cadence exists.

The agent MUST NOT end its turn while a process it is bound to observe is unfinished. A turn that ends hands the next observation to the operator's next message, which is the failure this rule exists to prevent. Between observations the agent either does other work or awaits one 60-second timer; it never waits idle without a timer and never stops.
An agent that starts a subagent MUST monitor it until it reaches a terminal state.

A fixed-cadence progress check MUST target only an asynchronous process that exposes an observation point while it runs. A background subagent and a background command with readable output are such processes.

The starting agent MUST drive each progress check from one single-shot timer it arms itself. The starting agent MUST NOT pre-schedule a series of ticks. A queued tick is delivered only when the session next takes a turn. A burst of queued ticks then arrives after the work it was meant to guard.
The timer payload is the sleep command line plus the arming record. The arming record MUST name the agents to inspect on wake and the check to run on each.

On each wake the starting agent MUST inspect every named agent's state. It MUST close the agents that reached a terminal state. While any awaited agent remains unfinished, it MUST arm exactly one successor timer at the cadence above. A stall is two consecutive wakes at which one agent shows unchanged state and no new output. The starting agent MUST stop re-arming for a stalled agent and MUST apply the recovery instruction below.

The single-shot timer MUST be a background shell sleep of the cadence length. The starting agent MUST then await that sleep with the platform's shell-await turn (AwaitShell in Cursor). The await keeps the agent's turn alive. It hands control back the moment the sleep returns. The check thus runs at the cadence rather than at the session's next turn.

The starting agent MUST NOT use a scheduled tick, an unawaited background sleep, or a foreground sleep as the timer: the first two are delivered only when the session next takes a turn, and the third blocks the operator conversation.
Inside a harness run the starting agent MUST use `pan watch <run-id>` as its timer and as its arming and wake record. It MUST NOT hand-arm sleeps for a run-scoped worker.

`pan watch` sleeps one cadence, inspects the invocation output and evidence paths, and appends each arming and wake to `agent/evidence/<invocation-id>-watch.jsonl`. The starting agent MUST await that command in the foreground until it exits.
`pan watch` defaults to a 60-second cadence for every worker. The starting agent MUST NOT pass `--cadence-seconds` unless the operator directs a different cadence.

The starting agent MUST treat a foreground worker call that the platform turns into a background launch as a background subagent at once. The starting agent MUST run `pan watch <run-id> --mark-background` immediately.
Platform text that says not to poll or await a background worker MUST NOT stop the watch. The hand-armed sleep instructions above apply only to an agent outside a harness run.

On each arming and each wake the starting agent MUST record the wall-clock time. The record MUST name the agents the arming record names and each agent's observed state. The starting agent MUST carry that record into its report. Without the record an agent that never armed anything and one that woke on schedule leave identical evidence.
A platform completion signal MAY end a wait early and MUST NOT replace the timer as the check mechanism. An agent that ends its turn to wait for such a signal has broken the 60-second rule.

A missed observation is a `DELEGATE-001` violation whatever the outcome of the process. The agent MUST record the miss, the interval it left unobserved, and the reason in its report or stage output, and MUST resume the cadence at once.

A foreground blocking call exposes no observation point, so no fixed cadence binds it. The starting agent MUST record launch evidence before the call. After the call returns it MUST record completion evidence with the elapsed time and a terminal-state inspection. Inside a harness run the completion evidence is `pan watch <run-id> --foreground-returned`. That command reads the launch clock from `agent/evidence/<invocation-id>-launch.json`; `--launched-at` supplies the observed launch time and writes that record when no watch armed first, while an arming without it records the arming time. The delegation artifact's modification time is neither a launch signal nor a progress signal. The starting agent MUST run the command at once when a foreground launch returns with the worker output present.
The starting agent owns the subagent outcome and MUST detect a crash, a stall, and a silent exit.
The starting agent MUST NOT depend on the subagent to report back, because a report is a convenience rather than a guarantee.
On a detected stall or crash, the starting agent MUST report the condition and MUST take or propose a recovery action.
An operator-facing agent MUST start a subagent or other asynchronous process in the background.
An operator-facing agent MUST NOT block the operator conversation on a foreground subagent call.
A supervisor MUST keep in-run worker delegation foreground and blocking, because it needs the worker result to advance the stage.

Worker model evidence is best-effort. When no probe answer lands, the harness MUST record the run snapshot's projected model as a labeled `default`, and every display MUST distinguish that projected default from a probed `match` or `recorded` result. A probed model that contradicts the run snapshot remains a hard `MODEL_EVIDENCE_MISMATCH` failure.

Agent nesting MUST NOT exceed two levels: top level → child agent → subagent, and no further. A child agent MAY spawn subagents only for auxiliary work that is not a stage delegation (repository exploration, debugging). Such nested spawns always run the platform default model. A second-level subagent MUST NOT spawn anything.

For a worker invocation that an operator session delegated, `pan submit` MUST require a completed watch record or a foreground-return attestation. Without one it MUST fail with `DELEGATION_UNOBSERVED`, not an advisory. A worker the harness delegated is exempt only when its harness-authored delegation execution record names the run and invocation.

A watch MAY record `completed` when agent state is `completed`, or when the output is plausible after one cadence elapsed since launch. When agent state is not `completed`, output within one cadence MUST NOT complete the watch. Output plausibility alone carries a false-positive risk: a worker can write a complete-looking output and continue editing.
Every completed watch wake MUST record `terminal_basis` as `agent_state` or `output_plausible`.

A supervisor of several concurrent runs, such as a cohort session, MUST launch the ready worker of each distinct run in one message. The platform then runs the launches in parallel, and each call stays foreground. It MUST NOT launch two workers for one run and MUST NOT exceed the cohort's recorded parallelism limit. When the platform converts one such launch into a background subagent, the supervisor MUST run `pan watch <run-id> --mark-background` for that run at once. The supervisor MUST then await the outstanding watches together.

instructions.text: The harness MUST preserve the existing launch clock when `--mark-background` re-arms a watch; coverage: `tests/integration/watch.test.ts::a mark-background re-arm preserves the existing launch clock`.
